result.title: Causal Diffusion for Extreme Super-Resolution in Interactive Games
result.summary: Existing game super-resolution methods typically operate at moderate upscaling factors, struggling to recover fine visual details from extremely low-resolution inputs (e.g., 120p). At such resolutions, super-resolution shifts from reconstructing existing information toward synthesizing missing visual details. While video diffusion models offer powerful generative priors for this challenging task, their dependence on future frames limits their applicability to interactive games. We present CIDER, a causal diffusion framework for extreme game super-resolution that synthesizes high-frequency details from current and past low-resolution frames, guided by G-buffers (depth and motion vectors) to preserve scene structure and temporal consistency. We collect data from two AAA games (Cyberpunk 2077 and Black Myth: Wukong). To reduce inference load, we develop a lightweight latent projection encoder tailored to ultra-low-resolution inputs, fine-tune a decoder (TAE) on our high-resolution outputs, and distill the diffusion model to reach interactive frame rates. Our experiments demonstrate high-fidelity 8$\times$ upscaling from 120p to 960p at around 13 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art game upscalers in visual quality and showing potential for 16$\times$ magnification.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CIDER，一个面向交互式游戏的因果扩散超分框架，仅用当前与历史低分辨率帧和深度、运动矢量引导，从 120p 合成 960p 高频细节，并通过轻量编码器、解码器微调与蒸馏达到约 13 FPS。
AI.relevance_reason: 属图像/视频生成式的画质增强工作，「causal」仅指时间上不使用未来帧，与 LVR 关注的内部推理状态、证据获取或停止决策无实质联系，也无具体可借鉴线索。
